tools.name: get_business
tools.description: Read the business card: what it is, where the work happens, its hours and time zone, its services with prices and lengths, what a booking needs (the customer's details and the questions to answer), whether a booking is confirmed at once or sent as a request, the limits and the cancel rule. Call it f

tools.name: find_times
tools.description: Find the start times that are open for what is being booked, between two dates (at most 14 days). Pass `windows` (the customer's free time from their calendar) to get only the starts that fit both calendars. Returns ISO 8601 times with offsets. Only open times are ever shown.

tools.name: check_address
tools.description: For a business that comes to the customer: check the service address before booking. Send it as one line, as fields, or as a place_id saved from an earlier check. The answer says whether Google confirmed it (`verdict`), the address to book with (send it as answers.address), its place_id (save both f

tools.name: book
tools.description: Book one of the open times for the customer. The business then either confirms it at once or receives it as a request it approves (or, for a business that takes its bookings by email, confirms with the customer itself); the answer says which, what happens next, and a `manage.token` to check or cance

tools.name: get_booking
tools.description: Check a booking made through this door: whether it is requested, confirmed, declined or cancelled, and whether it can still be cancelled here.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Cancel a booking made through this door: withdraws a request still waiting, or cancels a booking the business confirmed at once. A booking the business has approved must be changed with the business directly (the answer says how). Ask the customer first.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: book · Private data: book · Public sink: check_address, book.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: book · Private data: book · Public sink: check_address, book

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
